name: Negroni
description: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth—bitter, aromatic, and built for slow sipping.
history: Credited to Florence in the early 20th century as a stiffening of the Americano. The equal-parts build is the modern standard.
whyItWorks: Campari’s bitterness, vermouth’s sweetness, and gin’s botanicals lock into a self-balancing triangle.
steps: Add gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth to a rocks glass with a large cube.
Stir briefly to chill and integrate.
Express an orange peel over the drink and place it in the glass.
techniqueNotes: Build in the glass for ease, or stir in a mixing glass for extra polish.
If too bitter, nudge vermouth up by ¼ oz.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Tea and spice notes stand up beautifully to Campari.
Clean juniper keeps the bitter profile focused.
Softer floral gin for a gentler Negroni.

variations.name: Boulevardier
variations.notes: Replace gin with bourbon or rye.
